title: Agents Are Where Microservices Were in 2015 — Roberto Milev & Uday Kanagala, Navan
talk_summary: Navan's architecture team describes a layered production agent stack (runtime, memory, context, observability, guardrails, orchestration) and argues most layers are immature except runtime and tool calling. The most concrete transferable ideas are skill-based context composition, hook-based tracing of agent decisions, trajectory-based evals, and pre/post-tool-call guardrails.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat a 'skill' as a pluggable unit combining instructions/domain context plus tool execution, compose context dynamically per task, and use progressive disclosure to start narrow and expand via metadata.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we compose context dynamically out of skills that we use as units of work that are pluggable, that we can test independently, and that we can reuse

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of trying to force a deterministic graph, they record the agent's actual trajectory from start to goal and score how far it diverged, plus flag inferred vs. grounded answers as regression signals.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Can we have a trajectory of its starting from an end to a goal and then see how much how far it went in the trajectory

takeaways.what_they_do: They intercept pre/post tool calls and pre/post decisions via framework hooks to emit traces with goal, reasoning, belief status, tool calls, and a confidence score, rather than reading raw thinking logs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before pre-tool and post-tool call or a pre-decision or a post-decision, so all of that are a point point in time for us to intercept

takeaways.what_they_do: They run authorization and policy checks before and after every tool call, with fine-grained decisions for agents acting on behalf of users vs. service accounts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before every tool call pre-tool and post-tool, we have this guardrails to check and block and make a informed decisions

takeaways.technique: Single master agent with progressively loaded sub-skills
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately avoid multi-agent sprawl, using one master agent that decides which sub-skills/sub-agents to load per use case, and reserve A2A protocols for cross-team boundaries.
They flag unpredictable cost as unsolved and describe the direction of reliable fallback and using cheaper models for certain tasks, while warning vendors are incentivized to burn tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have agents be, uh, using cheaper models for certain tasks
